label: June 2026 paper — gap-fill practice variants (booklet Q1–Q50)

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ is a random sample from f(x; θ) = θe^(−θx), x > 0. For testing H₀: θ = θ₀ against H₁: θ > θ₀ at level α (χ²(α, ν) is the upper α point of χ² with ν df), the uniformly most powerful (UMP) critical region is
items.explanation: The family has a monotone likelihood ratio in −Σxᵢ, so for the one-sided H₁: θ > θ₀ a UMP test rejects for small Σxᵢ. Under H₀, 2θ₀ΣXᵢ ~ χ²(2n), so the cut-off is χ²(1−α, 2n)/(2θ₀) (the lower α point). Trap: a UMP test exists for one-sided alternatives in a family with a monotone likelihood ratio, but not for a two-sided one.

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ is a random sample from f(x; θ) = θe^(−θx), x > 0. For testing H₀: θ = θ₀ against H₁: θ < θ₀ at level α (χ²(α, ν) is the upper α point of χ² with ν df), the uniformly most powerful (UMP) critical region is
items.explanation: Smaller θ means larger observations, so the UMP test for H₁: θ < θ₀ rejects for large Σxᵢ; with 2θ₀ΣXᵢ ~ χ²(2n) under H₀ the cut-off is χ²(α, 2n)/(2θ₀). Trap: a UMP test exists for one-sided alternatives in a family with a monotone likelihood ratio, but not for a two-sided one.

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ is a random sample from N(μ, 1). For testing H₀: μ = μ₀ against H₁: μ ≠ μ₀ at level α, the uniformly most powerful (UMP) critical region is
items.explanation: The most powerful test against μ > μ₀ rejects for large X̄ and against μ < μ₀ for small X̄; no single test is best on both sides, so no UMP test exists (the two-sided test is UMP unbiased only). Trap: a UMP test exists for one-sided alternatives in a family with a monotone likelihood ratio, but not for a two-sided one.

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ is a random sample from Poisson(λ). For testing H₀: λ = λ₀ against H₁: λ > λ₀ at level α, the uniformly most powerful (UMP) critical region is
options: reject H₀ when Σxᵢ is far from nλ₀ on either side
reject H₀ for large Σxᵢ (randomizing at the boundary if needed)
items.explanation: The Poisson family has a monotone likelihood ratio in Σxᵢ, so by Karlin–Rubin the UMP test for the one-sided H₁: λ > λ₀ rejects for large Σxᵢ; randomization attains size α exactly. Trap: a UMP test exists for one-sided alternatives in a family with a monotone likelihood ratio, but not for a two-sided one.

items.stem: For testing H₀: θ ∈ Θ₀ against H₁: θ ∈ Θ₁ with Θ = Θ₀ ∪ Θ₁, the likelihood ratio statistic is λ = sup over Θ₀ of the likelihood divided by sup over Θ. Consider: A. 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1. B. −2 logₑ λ is asymptotically χ² under H₀, with degrees of freedom equal to the number of restrictions. C. λ can exceed 1 when H₀ is false. D. −2 logₑ λ ~ N(0, 1) asymptotically. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The numerator maximises over a subset of the parameter space, so it cannot exceed the denominator: 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 always (A true, C false). By Wilks' theorem −2 log λ is asymptotically χ² with df equal to the number of independent restrictions (B true, D false). Trap: the limit is χ², not normal.
